objectives.text: Can identify some known letters in words.
Can recognise the use of a question mark to signal a question.
Can recognise the letters of the alphabet in upper and lower case.
Can read cardinal numbers up to ten written as words.
Can point to the title of a book on a cover.
Can recognise cardinal numbers up to ten when written as words in short texts.
Can read a text in the correct direction, from left to right and from the top of the page to the bottom.
Can identify the initial sound in simple words.
Can recognise some words that are similar in their first language.
Can understand basic sentences introducing someone (e.g. ‘name’, ‘age’).
Can recognise a range of basic everyday nouns and adjectives (e.g. ‘colours’, ‘numbers’, ‘classroom objects’).
Can combine single letter sounds to read simple words.
Can recognise cardinal numbers up to 50 written as words.
Can recognise different basic words or phrases used for a similar purpose (e.g. ‘hi’ / ‘hello’) to greet someone.
Can understand basic time words e.g. ‘days of the week’, ‘months of the year.’
Can recognise familiar names, words and very basic phrases on simple notices and signs.
Can demonstrate understanding of a word by matching it to a picture.
Can recognise basic plural forms of common nouns (e.g. ‘cars’, ‘books’).
Can understand some simple, everyday signs (e.g. ‘car park’, ‘station’, ‘bathroom’).
Can understand very short, simple, instructions on everyday signs (e.g. ‘No parking’, ‘No food or drink’).
Can recognise some frequent everyday words.
Can recognise basic action words (e.g. ‘clap’, ‘stamp’, ‘jump’, ‘walk’).
Can identify the individual vowel and consonant sounds in simple words, if supported by pictures.
Can recognise single, familiar everyday words if supported by pictures.
Can hear the initial sound in simple words.
Can recognise cardinal numbers up to 10 in short phrases and sentences spoken slowly and clearly.
Can recognise the letters of the alphabet by their sounds.
Can respond to a request for a simple evaluation with a gesture (e.g. ‘thumbs up’).
Can understand the letters of the alphabet by their names.
Can recognise a few familiar everyday nouns and adjectives (e.g. ‘colours’, ‘numbers’, ‘classroom objects’), if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can understand some basic words and phrases to show politeness (e.g. ‘Please’, ‘Thank you’, ‘Excuse me’, ‘Sorry’).
Can understand a simple evaluation (e.g. ‘yes/no’, ‘good/bad’).
Can follow short, basic classroom instructions, if supported by pictures or gestures.
Can understand basic expressions for greeting and leave-taking, if supported by gestures.
Can understand basic action words (e.g. ‘clap’, ‘stamp’, ‘jump’, ‘walk’).
Can recognise isolated words related to familiar topics, if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by pictures or gestures.
Can understand simple negative instructions related to everyday situations (e.g. ‘Don’t run’), if supported by gestures.
Can hear the individual vowel and consonant sounds in simple words, if supported by pictures.
Can recognise familiar expressions used to signal the beginning and end of activities in the classroom.
Can understand a few basic words and phrases in a story that is read aloud to them.
Can recognise familiar words and phrases in short, simple songs or chants.
Can understand simple spoken commands as part of a game.
Can understand the time of day when expressed in full hours.
Can understand the main information when people introduce themselves (e.g. ‘name’, ‘age’, ‘where they are from’).
Can identify everyday objects, people or animals in their immediate surroundings or in pictures from short, basic descriptions (e.g. ‘colour’, ‘size’), if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can follow basic instructions to colour, draw or make something.
Can recognise familiar words in short phrases and sentences spoken slowly and clearly, if supported by pictures or gestures.
Can understand simple questions about personal information (e.g. ‘name’ or ‘age’) if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can understand short, simple instructions addressed slowly and clearly.
Can understand simple language related to naming and describing family members.
Can understand simple questions asking for basic information about objects in their immediate surroundings or in pictures (e.g. ‘colour’, ‘size’), if addressed slowly and clearly.
Can get the gist of a simple song, if supported by gestures.

lessons.title: Mia and Pip at the Zoo
